domain: Transportation Systems / Institutional Coordination / Technology Lock-In
topic_summary: Analysis of the convention determining which side of the road vehicles travel on, focusing on right-hand driving as the globally dominant standard. Examines the coordination mechanisms, path dependencies, and structural constraints that maintain this convention despite its arbitrary origins.

key_entities.name: Left-hand traffic countries
key_entities.role: Jurisdictions enforcing left-side driving convention (UK, Japan, Australia, etc.)

key_entities.name: Automotive manufacturers
key_entities.role: Producers of vehicles with fixed steering-wheel placement

key_entities.name: Border crossing infrastructure
key_entities.role: Physical transition points between different handedness regimes

key_entities.name: Drivers and pedestrians
key_entities.role: Agents whose coordination the convention enables

key_claims.content: The choice of right vs left has no inherent physical or safety advantage
Universal adoption within a jurisdiction prevents head-on collisions
Changing handedness requires simultaneous infrastructure and vehicle fleet replacement
Approximately 65-70% of world population drives on the right

key_tensions.nature: Adjacent jurisdictions with different conventions create coordination friction at borders
Minority markets face higher vehicle costs due to specialized production runs

key_mechanisms.description: State traffic law enforcement punishing wrong-side driving
Each additional adopter increases coordination value for all participants
Road signage, lane markings, intersection design physically encode handedness

key_absences.description: No analysis of whether pedestrian flow conventions (sidewalk passing) correlate with or diverge from vehicular handedness
No consideration of whether human visual/motor asymmetries (handedness, visual field dominance) create any measurable safety differential between conventions

axes.structural_delta: The convention solves a pure coordination problem where any universal standard has equal value but deviation is costly
axes.primary_observable: Accident rates at borders between different-handedness jurisdictions vs within-jurisdiction rates; switching costs measured in Sweden 1967 transition
axes.selection_reason: Foundational mountain providing the coordination substrate; feeds into both downstream axes

axes.structural_delta: Physical infrastructure (road design, signage, intersections) and vehicle fleet composition create switching costs that grow with network size
axes.primary_observable: Cost estimates for jurisdiction-wide handedness switches; infrastructure replacement timelines; vehicle fleet turnover rates
axes.selection_reason: Distinct observable (switching costs vs coordination value); rope mechanism layered on mountain substrate

axes.structural_delta: Left-hand traffic countries face higher vehicle costs due to specialized production runs and reduced economies of scale
axes.primary_observable: Price differential for LHT-spec vehicles vs RHT-spec vehicles; production volume ratios; manufacturer profit margins by market
axes.selection_reason: Distinct beneficiary structure; extractive mechanism downstream of both coordination and lock-in

omegas.description: Does human handedness or visual field dominance create any measurable safety differential between RHT and LHT? If so, the Mountain of coordination_equilibrium may conceal a weak Piton of biological optimization.

Do pedestrian flow conventions (sidewalk passing, stairwell traffic) follow vehicular handedness or diverge? Divergence would suggest the coordination equilibrium is domain-specific rather than universal.
Was LHT adoption in former British colonies a Rope (coordination) or a Snare (imposed extraction)? Post-independence retention suggests Rope, but transition costs may have locked in colonial choice.

fracture_scan.notes: No fractures detected. Three axes pass pairwise independence: coordination_equilibrium (different observable: coordination value vs switching costs), network_lock_in (different observable: infrastructure replacement costs vs coordination value), manufacturing_extraction (different observable: price differentials; distinct beneficiary structure). Dark matter probes surfaced cognitive asymmetry and pedestrian flow as bounded uncertainties rather than distinct axes.
